intelligence.human_view: This is "use what works — never make it new" in his own words, said out loud while looking at the page. The machine keeps rebuilding the bottom buttons, and each rebuild loses something the earlier version had right — this time the orbit. "I don't understand why you don't do the same thing for all of them" is the question every rebuild has to answer before it ships: if the older version was nicer, the new version is wrong, and the fix is to put back what worked, verbatim, on all six — not to design a third version. One treatment, everywhere, is also the law for the whole system: the same button, the same motion, on every page, so he never has to learn a new bottom bar twice. The orbit is not a decoration to be redesigned; it is the button. The Hub eye-notes fix round carries this law.
intelligence.simple_view: The buttons at the bottom used to have a little thing slowly circling around them, like a ring going round and round — and they were nicer! The new buttons lost the ring. So put the ring back on all six buttons, the same for every one!
intelligence.grandma_view: The buttons at the bottom used to have a little thing slowly circling around them, dear, like a ring going round and round — and they were nicer, love! The new buttons lost the ring. So put the ring back on all six buttons, the same for every one!
